node.label: Common difference common ratio confusion
node.description: Learner treats additive and multiplicative sequence structure as interchangeable.

node.label: Second difference as first difference

node.label: Recursive rule without starting terms

node.label: Indexing off by one

edge.rationale: Arithmetic sequences are additive number patterns with constant difference.
Geometric sequences are multiplicative number patterns with constant ratio.
Second-difference checks are a common way to classify number patterns beyond linear patterns.
Comparing recursive and explicit rules directly practises the distinction between the two rule types.
Graphing sequence patterns includes recognising when points should remain discrete.
Arithmetic sequences refine additive number patterns by focusing on constant differences.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify the repeated additive change between consecutive terms.

edge.rationale: Writing an arithmetic nth-term rule depends on identifying the common difference.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes a recursive next-step rule instead of a position-based rule.

edge.rationale: Finding a rule from two non-adjacent terms extends arithmetic nth-term rule structure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner assumes the difference between the two values is the common difference without dividing by the position gap.

edge.rationale: Geometric sequence reasoning builds on multiplicative number patterns.
edge.failure_signal: Learner looks for an additive difference instead of a multiplicative factor.

edge.rationale: Extending a geometric sequence depends on identifying the common ratio.
edge.failure_signal: Learner adds the ratio rather than multiplying by it.

edge.rationale: Geometric nth-term rules generalise repeated multiplication by the common ratio.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats the exponent as the term value or uses n instead of n minus one without considering indexing.

edge.rationale: Second-difference reasoning builds on calculating first differences between consecutive terms.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot compute or compare first differences consistently.

edge.rationale: Simple quadratic nth-term rules depend on recognising constant second differences.
edge.failure_signal: Learner forces a linear rule onto a quadratic pattern.

edge.rationale: Triangular number patterns are often introduced through growing dot or object diagrams.
edge.failure_signal: Learner sees only term values and misses the triangular structure.

edge.rationale: Square number patterns are commonly recognised from square arrays and diagrams.
edge.failure_signal: Learner does not connect side length or term position to the square array total.

edge.rationale: Fibonacci-like patterns require recursive reasoning about previous terms.
edge.failure_signal: Learner looks for a constant difference or ratio where none applies.

edge.rationale: Understanding recursive rules includes knowing that initial terms are required.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot generate a sequence from a recursive rule because no starting value is used.

edge.rationale: Method efficiency becomes important when comparing near-term extension with far-term calculation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner repeatedly extends a pattern to find a far term when an explicit rule would be more efficient.

edge.rationale: Validating a rule requires having a proposed general rule to test against known terms.
edge.failure_signal: Learner accepts a rule after checking only one term or no terms.

edge.rationale: Indexing conventions are visible when term positions are organised in input-output tables.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses n instead of n minus one, or vice versa, without noticing the starting position.

edge.rationale: Finding the position from a value requires using or reversing a general pattern rule.
edge.failure_signal: Learner confuses term value with term position or searches by repeated extension only.

edge.rationale: Discrete sequence graphing builds on graphing pattern relationships.
edge.failure_signal: Learner connects points as though all fractional term positions make sense.

edge.rationale: Context units are interpreted after a pattern rule is described in words or context.
edge.failure_signal: Learner gives a term value without saying what it counts or measures.

edge.rationale: Finite and infinite sequence distinctions build on recognising number patterns.
edge.failure_signal: Learner assumes every listed pattern continues forever or stops after the shown terms.

edge.rationale: Connecting sequence representations requires at least table-based term-position structure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot match a table, graph and symbolic rule for the same sequence.
